speaker: Doctor
text: Good day, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, could you please tell me when your baby was born and when you first noticed the fever and abdominal pain? I also need to know if you experienced any vaginal bleeding or had any complications during delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any burning or pain when you urinate, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? I will also need to check your vital signs and perform a pelvic exam to assess the extent of the uterine tenderness. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness, prolonged labor, and large infant, endometritis is highly likely despite the normal urinalysis. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual, as endometritis typically presents with leukocytosis. Do you have any history of a ruptured membrane or prolonged labor, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal labs and imaging, the fever and tenderness may be due to a localized soft tissue infection or thrombophlebitis. Do you have any pain in your legs, and have you noticed any redness or swelling in the perineal area? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and labs, we must consider rare causes like pelvic thrombophlebitis or an abscess not seen on CT. Does the fever spike in the evenings, and have you noticed any pain in your legs or a palpable cord-like structure in your pelvis? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the fever persists despite negative workup for infection and thrombophlebitis, I must consider septic pelvic thrombophlebitis which often presents with spiking fevers and a negative CT. Does your fever spike in the evenings, and have you noticed any pain in your legs or a palpable cord-like structure in your pelvis? DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis
